name: How does Colorado's dry climate affect trim repair and maintenance?

mainEntity.name: How does Colorado's dry climate affect trim repair and maintenance?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Colorado, dramatic seasonal humidity swings between dry winters and rainy spring months cause building materials to expand and contract significantly. This rapid movement often leads to cracked caulk lines, miter joint separation in crown molding, and nail pops along baseboards in communities from Aurora to Castle Rock. Standard rigid fillers can snap under this movement. Using flexible, elastomeric caulking and leaving proper expansion margins at joints prevents trim seams from reopening as indoor moisture levels shift with seasonal furnace and cooling use.
acceptedAnswer.description: Colorado's extreme indoor humidity shifts cause wood to expand and shrink, breaking rigid caulk. Using flexible sealants and secure nailing prevents joints from pulling apart.
